CVE-2026-96960 (GHSA-7hqp-7c5m-4vq6) is a .NET denial of service issue in signed XML processing (System.Security.Cryptography.Xml and System.Private.Xml), classed as asymmetric resource consumption, or amplification (CWE-405). Microsoft's fix for this group of signed-XML issues adds input-depth and operation-count limits, prohibits DTD processing by default, validates entity references, bounds encrypted-data candidate processing and caps the attributes and namespaces used by C14N transforms. Microsoft lists System.Security.Cryptography.Xml 8.0.0 through 8.0.4 as affected, fixed in 8.0.5, and the .NET 8.0.32 release notes list this CVE and System.Security.Cryptography.Xml 8.0.5 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7hqp-7c5m-4vq6, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/490, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.32/8.0.32.md). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold. System.Security.Cryptography.Xml implementation code is in the ASP.NET Core shared framework (aspnetcore8-runtime), in dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap, which holds the .NET SDK with its F# copy and shared frameworks and the ASP.NET Core Alpine runtime pack, and in dotnet8-runtime-artifacts, which holds the ASP.NET Core and Windows Desktop internal transport packages and the System.Security.Cryptography.Xml NuGet package. In every build each of these copies is built from that build's own .NET release: 8.0.23 to 8.0.31, with System.Security.Cryptography.Xml package 8.0.4 or earlier, in the first seven builds, and 8.0.32 or later, with package 8.0.5, from 8.0.32-r0 on. dotnet8-runtime-artifacts also holds older System.Security.Cryptography.Xml versions (4.7.1, 6.0.1 and 7.0.1, and copies inside .NET build-tool packages) only as source-build reference assemblies, which carry no implementation code. In dotnet8-runtime, dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap and dotnet8-runtime-artifacts, System.Xml implementation code (System.Private.Xml.dll) is in the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework in dotnet8-runtime and, in dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap, in the .NET SDK's shared framework, the Alpine runtime pack and the NativeAOT ILCompiler package; in every build each copy reports that build's own .NET version, 8.0.23 to 8.0.31 in the first seven builds and 8.0.32 or later from 8.0.32-r0 on. The range ends at 8.0.32-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix. No 8.0.28 or 8.0.30 build was published for Alpine 3.23.

DHI dotnet8-sdk for Alpine 3.23 builds the .NET 8 SDK for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET SDK version it carries. We read every package built from the dotnet8-sdk source for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository, x86_64 and aarch64: dotnet8-sdk, dotnet8-sdk-dbg, dotnet8-templates, netstandard21-targeting-pack, dotnet-doc, dotnet-bash-completion and dotnet-zsh-completion in the 9 published builds 8.0.123-r0, 8.0.124-r0, 8.0.125-r0, 8.0.126-r0, 8.0.127-r0, 8.0.129-r0, 8.0.131-r0, 8.0.133-r0 and 8.0.134-r0 (no 8.0.128, 8.0.130 or 8.0.132 build is published for Alpine 3.23), each download matching its index checksum, recursing into the zip and NuGet archives they hold, and read the version resources of every System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll and System.Private.Xml.dll; both architectures match in every build. Each dotnet8-sdk package holds two implementation copies of System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll, in the SDK root and FSharp directories under /usr/lib/dotnet/sdk/<version>. dotnet8-sdk-dbg holds debugging symbols (.pdb files) for System.Security.Cryptography.Xml and System.Private.Xml but no code for either, and no package built from this source, nor any archive inside one, holds any other System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll or any System.Private.Xml.dll file. Symbolic links with those names, such as the ones in the dotnet8-sdk runtime-pack directories under /usr/lib/dotnet/packs, point into /usr/lib/dotnet/shared, where no package built from this source installs either file; they are not copies and were not counted. In every build both copies report the .NET runtime version of that SDK release and name the dotnet/runtime commit they were built from: 8.0.23, 8.0.24, 8.0.25, 8.0.26, 8.0.27, 8.0.29 and 8.0.31 in the builds up to 8.0.131-r0, built from the v8.0.23 to v8.0.31 tag commits, which do not contain 8863b0e, and 8.0.33 and 8.0.34 in 8.0.133-r0 and 8.0.134-r0, built from the v8.0.33 and v8.0.34 tag commits, which do. The range ends at 8.0.133-r0, the first published build with the fix.

Microsoft lists System.Security.Cryptography.Xml 8.0.0 through 8.0.4 as affected, fixed in 8.0.5, and the .NET 8.0.32 release, whose SDKs are 8.0.426 and 8.0.132, lists this CVE and System.Security.Cryptography.Xml 8.0.5: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-7hqp-7c5m-4vq6, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/490, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.32/8.0.32.md. Microsoft names no commit per CVE. In dotnet/runtime the signed-XML fixes reached the release/8.0 branch in merge commit 8863b0e, "[release/8.0] Signed CMS and Signed XML fixes (10B)", which brings in 3e25a0e, "Apply Encrypted XML and Signed CMS security fixes", and 76a522b, "Bound encrypted data candidate processing"; it is in the v8.0.32 tag and not in v8.0.31: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/commit/8863b0e2dd554a5d2abed4a43a628bc872d6321b, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/commit/3e25a0e2f21a6fa1ab71ea2c8a84eea3728cd129, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/commit/76a522b8158af872da6c787e2122a7ac780e3192. DHI dotnet-sdk-8 for Debian 13 repackages Microsoft's .NET 8 SDK. We read every package built from the dotnet-sdk-8 source in the DHI Debian repository, amd64 and arm64: dotnet-sdk-8 and dotnet-sdk-8-oci-config in the 10 published builds 8.0.422-0 to the current 8.0.428-1, each download matching its index checksum, recursing into the zip and NuGet archives they hold, and read the version resources of every System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll and System.Private.Xml.dll; both architectures match in every build. No debug-symbol packages are published for this source, and each dotnet-sdk-8-oci-config package holds only two files, a YAML configuration file and its changelog. Every dotnet-sdk-8 build carries System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll in the ASP.NET Core shared framework under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App/<version> and in the SDK root, FSharp and dotnet-watch directories under /usr/lib/dotnet/sdk/<version>; 8.0.422-0 and 8.0.423-0 also carry a copy in the dotnet-format tool directory. System.Private.Xml.dll is in the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.NETCore.App/<version>. Each build also has a System.Security.Cryptography.Xml reference assembly under packs/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref, metadata without implementation used only at compile time. In 8.0.422-0 to 8.0.425-1 every implementation copy is older than the fix. The System.Security.Cryptography.Xml implementation copies report product version 8.0.26 in 8.0.422-0, whose dotnet-format copy is 8.0.0, and 8.0.29 (file version 8.0.2926.32403, the version of the assembly in the System.Security.Cryptography.Xml 8.0.4 NuGet package) in 8.0.423-0 to 8.0.425-1, except the 8.0.423-0 dotnet-format copy, which is 8.0.26; System.Private.Xml reports 8.0.28 to 8.0.31. From 8.0.426-0 on, every System.Security.Cryptography.Xml implementation copy reports 8.0.32 (file version 8.0.3226.50405, the version of the assembly in the fixed 8.0.5 NuGet package), and System.Private.Xml reports 8.0.32, 8.0.33 or 8.0.34. Each copy's version string also names the dotnet/runtime commit it was built from: the v8.0.0, v8.0.26 and v8.0.28 to v8.0.31 tag commits, none of which contains 8863b0e, in the builds up to 8.0.425-1, and the v8.0.32, v8.0.33 and v8.0.34 tag commits, which all contain it, from 8.0.426-0 on. The range ends at 8.0.426-0, the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-96960 (GHSA-7hqp-7c5m-4vq6): signed-XML processing in System.Security.Cryptography.Xml and System.Private.Xml lacked input-depth and operation-count limits, allowed DTD processing by default, did not validate entity references and did not bound encrypted-data candidates or the attributes and namespaces used by C14N transforms, so crafted XML could exhaust CPU and memory (denial of service). Microsoft fixes it in System.Security.Cryptography.Xml 9.0.21 and in the .NET 9.0.21 release (runtime 9.0.21, SDK 9.0.319 and 9.0.122): https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-7hqp-7c5m-4vq6, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/490, https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-96960, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.21/9.0.21.md. We unpacked every published dotnet-sdk-9 package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository, amd64 and arm64, from 9.0.315-0 to the current 9.0.321-1, and read the product version of every System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll and System.Private.Xml.dll (the SDK directory, F#, dotnet-format, dotnet-watch, the ASP.NET Core shared framework and reference pack, and the bundled Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework) in each; in 9.0.318-1 for amd64 we also opened the .zip and .nupkg archives the package carries and found no further copy. The dotnet-sdk-9-oci-config package built from the same source holds only a configuration file and its changelog (checked in 9.0.315-0 and 9.0.321-1). Each copy carries the .NET runtime version of the SDK release it ships with: 9.0.318-1 and every earlier build carry 9.0.20 or older, inside the affected range, while 9.0.319-0 and every later build carry 9.0.21 or newer, which contain the fix. The range ends at 9.0.319-0.
